samples.question: The picture shows a plain background with a number of dark round blobs and nothing else. Exactly one blob, the hub, is much larger than the others; all the remaining blobs are dots of one and the same size. Every dot sits at a different distance from the hub, so the dots can be put in one order by walking outward from the hub, from the nearest dot to the farthest dot. Following that outward order, the direction from the hub to the dot keeps turning the same way around the hub, by a similar amount at every step and always by less than a quarter turn, so the dots trace a single chain that winds outward around the hub. Turning as the hands of a clock printed on this picture would turn counts as clockwise. The number of dots, the size of the blobs, the position of the hub in the frame, the direction in which the chain starts, the amount of dark ink and how far apart the dots are all carry no information about the answer. Walking outward from the hub, which way does the chain of dots wind? Answer clockwise or counter-clockwise.
